text: Async in doeff is made of effects, too: Spawn, Wait, Gather, Race and Cancel.
scheduled wraps your program in one more handler layer: the scheduler. Like any handler, it gets each effect, and k, the rest of the program.
Spawn travels out to the scheduler, and the scheduler answers with a Task handle.
Spawn starts a task and hands back its handle. The task runs until it waits, and then main goes on.
Each task waits on the virtual clock, its k parked by wake-up time. They finish in time order: B, C, then A.
Gather waits for all three, and returns their values in input order: A, B, C.
The scheduler runs one task at a time, on one thread.
A task runs until it waits. These two never wait, so A runs all its steps before B starts.
Wait after each step, and the scheduler parks that k and resumes the next ready one: A1, B1, A2, B2.
Gather is fail-fast. B raises at one second, and Gather raises right then.
It cancels nothing. C still finishes at two seconds, and main can still wait for it.
Race returns the first value to finish: B. The loser, A, runs on until you cancel it.
Cancel is an effect too. yield Cancel, with the task, asks it to stop, and returns at once.
The task receives a Task Cancelled Error right where it waits, so its finally block runs.
Cleanup may perform effects. Wait on the task answers only after the cleanup is done.
doeff: a task is a paused program, and the scheduler is a handler that decides when each one resumes. pip install doeff.
